question: A mother with no family history of bleeding disorders has two sons diagnosed with Hemophilia A. Testing shows the mother has normal Factor VIII levels. Which of the following statements best explains the occurrence of the disease in both siblings?

answers.option: It is a non-genetic disease caused by somatic mutation
The children should be rechecked for an alternate diagnosis
The mother likely has germline mosaicism, and recurrence is possible
The inheritance pattern is Autosomal Recessive
The sons actually have Hemophilia B

question: A child presents with hypopigmented "ash-leaf" macules on the chest and angiofibromas on the face. An EEG is performed due to seizure activity and demonstrates hypsarrhythmia (associated with West syndrome). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old child presents with progressive proximal muscle weakness and difficulty climbing stairs. Physical examination reveals violaceous papules over the knuckles (Gottron papules), some of which show signs of calcinosis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-month-old infant presents with shortness of breath and poor feeding. On examination, the infant is not cyanotic (O2​ saturation 95%), but the liver is palpable 3 cm below the costal margin. A Grade 3/6 pansystolic murmur is heard at the left lower sternal border, radiating across the entire precordium. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A child with known Hemophilia A who has been receiving prophylactic Factor VIII replacement therapy presents with recurrent painful joint swelling (hemarthrosis). Despite adequate dosing, the treatment seems less effective. Which of the following should be assessed next?

An infant is brought to the clinic with a bright red rash in the diaper area. The rash involves the skin folds and is characterized by erythematous plaques with pinpoint "satellite" pustules at the edges. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

A mother brings her two children to the clinic. The first child has a persistent diaper rash and a crusted, honey-colored yellow rash on the face. The second child presents with a red, weeping lesion in the diaper area. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis considering the contagious nature and clinical presentation?

A child attended a party and consumed an unknown food item. Shortly after, the child developed sudden shortness of breath, swelling of the lips (angioedema), and petechiae. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-day-old neonate is screened for thyroid function, revealing a markedly elevated TSH of 2050 mIU/L. The pregnancy was uncomplicated, the mother is healthy, and the neonate appears physically well on examination with no palpable goiter. Which of the following is the most common cause of congenital hypothyroidism in this scenario?

answers.option: Transplacental passage of maternal antithyroid antibodies
Thyroid dysgenesis (e.g., ectopic thyroid or hypoplasia)

question: A mother who follows a strict vegan diet is exclusively breastfeeding her infant. Laboratory evaluation of the infant reveals a high MCV (macrocytosis) and hypersegmented neutrophils on a peripheral smear. Which of the following is the most likely cause of these hematologic findings?

answers.option: Decreased maternal intake of Vitamin B12
Decreased maternal intake of folic acid

question: A 5-year-old child presents for a wellness check. The parents report a sedentary lifestyle characterized by frequent fast-food consumption and excessive screen time. Which of the following is the most appropriate tool to assess this child's nutritional status and screen for obesity?

answers.option: Body Mass Index (BMI) for age percentiles

question: A 12-year-old child with a sedentary lifestyle and a diet consisting primarily of junk food is found to have a BMI of 22 kg/m2 (which is high for his age/sex percentile). Both parents have type 2 diabetes, and the child has recently experienced rapid weight gain. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

answers.option: Decrease caloric intake without further testing
Reassurance that the BMI is within a normal adult range
Check HbA1c to screen for type 2 diabetes

question: A child presents with a history of persistent polyuria and polydipsia. Laboratory evaluation reveals a random blood sugar of 110 mg/dL and a serum sodium level of 155 mEq/L. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's clinical presentation?

A 6-month-old infant is diagnosed with West syndrome based on the clinical presentation of infantile spasms and an EEG showing hypsarrhythmia. Which of the following is considered a first-line pharmacological treatment for this condition?

A 14-year-old girl presents with fluctuating ptosis and generalized muscle weakness that worsens toward the end of the day. In the absence of acetylcholine receptor antibody testing, which of the following is the most sensitive electrophysiological test to confirm a diagnosis of Myasthenia Gravis?

A 6-month-old boy presents with a history of recurrent diarrheal infections and persistent oral thrush since birth. Laboratory evaluation shows a normal total leukocyte count, but the differential count reveals 90% neutrophils and only 10% lymphocytes (significant lymphopenia). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-day-old infant has not yet passed meconium and presents with progressive abdominal distension and bilious vomiting. A barium enema reveals a microcolon. There is no explosive passage of stool upon digital rectal examination. Given the findings and a positive family history of respiratory issues, what is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old child presents with a 3-month history of low-grade fever, generalized lymphadenopathy, and significant weight loss. On examination, the child is emaciated and pale, with palpable hepatosplenomegaly. The family history reveals that the grandmother recently died after having similar symptoms. What is the most likely diagnosis?

During a well-child visit, an infant is observed to roll over and sit steadily without support. The infant is also able to transfer a small toy from one hand to the other. At approximately what age are these specific motor and coordinative milestones typically achieved?

A 10-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department immediately after eating fish at a restaurant. He has developed widespread urticaria, swelling of the lips, and inspiratory stridor. What is the most appropriate first-line pharmacological intervention for this patient?

A 19-year-old male presents with a 4-day history of progressive, symmetric, ascending muscle weakness and absent deep tendon reflexes. He is diagnosed with Guillain-Barré Syndrome. Which of the following is the most appropriate first-line treatment to hasten recovery?

A 5-year-old child is brought to the emergency department in the midst of a generalized tonic-clonic seizure that has lasted 20 minutes. Rectal diazepam was administered by paramedics 10 minutes ago without effect. After ensuring the airway is secure and establishing intravenous access, what is the next best step in management?

answers.option: Immediate intubation and induction of general anesthesia
Give a second dose of IV diazepam (or lorazepam)
Load with IV fosphenytoin or phenobarbital

question: An 8-year-old boy is brought to the clinic with a 3-day history of high-grade fever, vomiting, and pain in the right upper quadrant of his abdomen. His parents mention that the family recently went on a camping trip where the child drank water from a nearby stream. On physical examination, the child appears ill and has a tender, palpable liver edge 4 cm below the costal margin. Laboratory investigations reveal moderately elevated serum transaminases (AST and ALT). Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old child with cerebral palsy is evaluated for developmental progress. Clinical observation shows the child has achieved stable head control and can sit with external support, but cannot yet sit independently. The child is also able to transfer objects from one hand to the other. Based on these specific motor and manipulative milestones, what is the child's approximate developmental age?

An infant is born with multiple congenital anomalies including microcephaly, a prominent occiput, micrognathia (small jaw), and low-set malformed ears. Physical examination reveals clenched fists with the index finger overlapping the third finger, and "rocker-bottom" feet. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A child is brought to the clinic with a history of acute diarrhea. On assessment according to IMNCI (Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illness) guidelines, the child has very sunken eyes and the skin pinch goes back very slowly (more than 2 seconds). The child is lethargic and unable to drink. What is the most appropriate management?

answers.option: Manage with Plan B (Oral Rehydration Therapy in clinic)
Manage with Plan C (IV fluids/Ringer's Lactate) and give Zinc
Give oral antibiotics and send home
Relieve sore throat symptoms and follow up in 2 days

question: A partially vaccinated child presents with a 3-day history of high-grade fever, followed by vomiting and abdominal pain for 2 days. Physical examination reveals a non-blanching macular rash and signs of systemic illness. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old child presents with coarse facial features, including a large skull with heavy eyebrows, a broad thick nose, and corneal clouding (opaque corneas). Other findings include a short neck, lumbodorsal kyphosis, hepatosplenomegaly, an umbilical hernia, and broad hands. The child also exhibits significant developmental delay. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 10-year-old child presents with persistent pain and swelling in the small joints of both hands and feet, specifically involving the proximal and distal interphalangeal joints. On examination, more than five joints are affected symmetrically. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old child presents with swollen, painful joints (dactylitis). A sibling has a history of similar complaints. Hemoglobin electrophoresis reveals HbF at 70%, with the remainder being HbA and HbA2​. Notably, the child has never received a blood transfusion. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-month-old infant is brought to the clinic with an itchy rash involving the face, scalp, and extremities, but notably sparing the diaper area. The father has a history of allergic rhinitis, and a 5-year-old sibling has similar skin issues. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-month-old infant presents with a runny nose, cough, and progressive shortness of breath. Both the father and an older sibling recently had similar upper respiratory symptoms. Physical examination reveals wheezing and fine crackles. A chest X-ray shows hyperinflation of the lungs and patchy infiltrates. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old child is brought to the emergency department with a sudden onset of high-grade fever, sore throat, and significant drooling of saliva. The child appears toxic and prefers to sit leaning forward in a "tripod" position. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause?

A 6-year-old child presents with generalized edema (anasarca). Urinalysis reveals 3+ protein but no red cell casts. Laboratory tests show a serum albumin level of less than 2.5 g/dL and mild anemia. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old child is brought to the emergency department after ingesting unknown tablets. The child presents with hematuria, flank pain, and is now anuric (urine output 0.3 mL/kg/hr). His baseline creatinine was 0.6 mg/dL, but it has risen to 1.6 mg/dL within 4 hours. Laboratory results also show a serum potassium of 6.5 mEq/L and granular casts on urinalysis. According to the KDIGO clinical practice guidelines for AKI, what is the most likely stage of this injury?

A 3-year-old child is brought to the emergency department one hour after accidentally ingesting half a bottle of paracetamol syrup. The child is currently stable, conscious, and following commands. What is the most appropriate immediate management step for this patient?

A child with a known diagnosis of Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) has been experiencing a persistent fever for one month despite being on various antibiotics. He is now brought to the hospital after a sudden episode of seizures. On examination, his GCS is 13/15 and there is a rash on his lower extremities. What is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old child is brought to the emergency department with a 5-day history of fever, a single episode of seizures, and altered consciousness since this morning. On examination, the GCS is 7/15, signs of meningeal irritation (Brudzinski/Kernig) are positive, and there is a prominent purpuric rash on the legs and back. What is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old child presents with progressive weakness in both legs. Physical examination reveals symmetrical muscle bulk, significant hypotonia, and absent or "downgoing" (normal plantar) reflexes. There is no evidence of spasticity or hyperreflexia. Which of the following is the most likely site of the lesion?

A 3-month-old infant is brought to the clinic because he frequently "spits up" or regurgitates small amounts of milk shortly after feeding. The infant is otherwise healthy, gaining weight appropriately, and shows no signs of distress or respiratory complications. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?

answers.option: Positioning the baby upright after feeds and reassurance
Immediate change to an amino-acid-based formula

question: An 8-year-old child is evaluated for asthma control. The parents report that the child experiences symptoms 2 to 3 times a week, which has a slight impact on his daily play activities. He also wakes up at night due to coughing or wheezing 2 to 3 times a month. How would you classify his asthma severity?

A 5-year-old child presents with signs of high-output heart failure, generalized edema, and significant muscle cramps. On further history, the child’s diet is found to consist almost exclusively of polished white rice. Which of the following nutrient deficiencies is the most likely cause of this "wet beri-beri" presentation?

A child with a history of chronic suppurative otitis media (CSOM) presents with a high-grade fever, severe headache, and a ring-enhancing lesion on CT scan, confirming a brain abscess. Which of the following is the most appropriate empirical antibiotic regimen?

A 10-year-old child presents with a 2-day history of worsening headache and an altered state of consciousness. He developed a high-grade fever today and had a generalized seizure this morning. On examination, there are no signs of meningeal irritation, but upper motor neuron (UMN) signs are present. Imaging shows evidence of mild cerebral edema. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-year-old boy is brought to the clinic because he is significantly shorter than his classmates. His parents are of average height. On assessment, he has a normal IQ, normal facial features, and participates fully in school activities. A hand X-ray reveals that his bone age is delayed compared to his chronological age. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

answers.option: Constitutional delay of growth and puberty

question: A child is brought to the emergency department in severe respiratory distress. Physical examination reveals that the trachea is deviated to the left, breath sounds are absent on the right side, and percussion of the right chest is hyperresonant. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 10-year-old child presents with complaints of intermittent leg pain during exercise. On examination, the clinician notes a blood pressure of 145/90 mm Hg in the right arm. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in the clinical evaluation?

answers.option: Take blood pressure in the right leg only
Order an immediate CT scan of the head
Take pulses and blood pressure in all four limbs

question: A neonate is born via spontaneous vaginal delivery with meconium-stained liquor. The delivery is otherwise uneventful; the baby starts crying vigorously with minimal stimulation within one minute of birth and exhibits brisk reflexes. Which of the following best describes this neonate's condition?

A mother brings her 7-year-old son to the psychiatry clinic. She reports that he consistently fails to complete his school assignments, cannot remain seated for more than a few minutes, and frequently gets into physical altercations with his classmates. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A toddler is found in a storage room having ingested an unknown substance, believed to be a "long-acting" anticoagulant rat poison. The child is currently stable. Which of the following complications is most likely to develop over the next 24 to 72 hours?

answers.option: Hematuria, petechiae, and acute renal failure

question: A child is brought to the outpatient department with a history of progressive lethargy. On examination, the child is found to have female internal organs (ovaries and uterus present). Laboratory investigations reveal a serum sodium of 155 mEq/L and a serum potassium of 3.1 mEq/L. Based on the electrolyte profile and clinical presentation, which of the following is a possible diagnosis?

A mother brings her infant to the clinic expressing concern that the child's head size is not developing properly. Upon anthropometric measurement, the head circumference is plotted between the 50th and 90th centiles for age and sex. The child is meeting all developmental milestones. What is the most appropriate next step?

answers.option: Refer to neurosurgery for a shunt evaluation
Perform a thorough neurological examination and plot on growth chart over time
Immediately check for papilledema with fundoscopy
Order a CT or MRI of the head to rule out hydrocephalus
Reassure the mother as the measurement is within normal limits

question: A 3-year-old child, who is fully vaccinated according to the national schedule, falls while playing and sustains a minor superficial cut on the knee and a small scratch on the hand. The wounds are clean. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

answers.option: Administer tetanus toxoid vaccine plus tetanus immunoglobulins
Administer tetanus toxoid now and a booster in 4 weeks
Reassure the parents and perform local wound care
Administer a full 3-dose course of tetanus toxoid

question: A 12-year-old girl has been taking oral isotretinoin for severe acne. She presents with dry skin, cracked lips (cheilitis), and thinning hair. On examination, she complains of a persistent headache and blurred vision; fundoscopy reveals papilledema, suggestive of pseudotumor cerebri (idiopathic intracranial hypertension). What is the most appropriate management?

answers.option: Switch her to a different class of oral retinoids
Perform emergency neurosurgery to decompress the cerebral edema
Give dexamethasone to rapidly decrease intracranial pressure
Stop the isotretinoin immediately and monitor her symptoms
Supplement with high doses of Vitamin C and Vitamin E

question: A neonate is born via spontaneous vaginal delivery and appears healthy. Twelve hours later, the infant is noted to be vomiting small amounts of blood (hematemesis) and has passed a small amount of blood per rectum. The baby remains hemodynamically stable and the maternal nipples are intact. Which of the following is the most likely cause?

answers.option: Hemorrhagic disease of the newborn (Vitamin K deficiency)
Maternal ingestion of blood during delivery/swallowed maternal blood

question: A neonate is born with ambiguous genitalia. An urgent pelvic ultrasound reveals the presence of a uterus and ovaries. Laboratory investigations show a serum potassium (K+) of 5.9 mEq/L and a serum sodium (Na+) of 122 mEq/L. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 10-week-old infant is brought to the clinic for his second dose of the pentavalent vaccine. The physician reviews the reaction to the 6-week dose. Which of the following documented reactions constitutes an absolute contraindication to receiving a subsequent dose of a pertussis-containing vaccine?

answers.option: Mild redness at the injection site

question: A 6-month-old infant with Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) is brought to the emergency department with profound cyanosis and an SpO2​ of 78% that does not improve with supplemental oxygen. The infant is extremely irritable and hyperpneic. What is the most appropriate immediate pharmacological intervention to increase pulmonary blood flow?

answers.option: Administration of IV morphine and knee-chest positioning

question: A 12-year-old boy presents with occasional headaches and pain in his legs during physical education class. On examination, his systemic and neurological findings are normal, but his upper extremity blood pressure is >99th percentile for his age. Femoral pulses are markedly diminished or absent. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old child is brought to the ER within 30 minutes of ingesting an unknown liquid in the garage. The child has pinpoint pupils (miosis), excessive salivation, lacrimation, and visible muscle fasciculations. Which of the following is the most appropriate management strategy?

answers.option: Atropine followed by pralidoxime after 12 hours

question: A 7-year-old child presents to the emergency department in status asthmaticus. He is using accessory muscles, has a silent chest on auscultation, and is unable to speak in full sentences. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?

answers.option: Oxygen via mask with nebulized salbutamol and IV corticosteroids
Oxygen via mask with IV terbutaline and IV corticosteroids

question: A 2-year-old child is brought to the clinic with a "barking" cough, hoarseness, and inspiratory stridor that worsens when the child is agitated. Which of the following organisms is the most common cause of this clinical syndrome?

A 6-year-old child is brought to the emergency department after being bitten on the leg by a stray dog. After thorough wound cleansing, the physician decides to initiate the post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) vaccine series. According to the current WHO and CDC guidelines for immunocompetent individuals, which of the following is the standard 4-dose intramuscular schedule?

A 4-hour-old neonate, born at home with the assistance of a traditional birth attendant (dai), is brought to the hospital. The infant is lethargic with swollen eyes and a diffuse, fluctuant scalp swelling that crosses the suture lines. The anterior fontanelle is flat. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old child with a 2-day history of severe vomiting and diarrhea is brought to the ER. On examination, the child is lethargic, has a capillary refill time of 4 seconds, and a blood pressure of 78/60 mm Hg. What is the most appropriate initial fluid resuscitation step?

answers.option: 20 mL/kg Normal Saline bolus over 5–10 minutes
Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) via nasogastric tube

question: Following a routine vaccination visit, a mother reports that her infant experienced high-pitched crying (persistent inconsolable crying) and a brief episode of decreased muscle tone and responsiveness (hypotonic-hyporesponsive episode). Which component of the combination vaccine is most frequently associated with these neurological adverse events?

A 5-year-old child is recovering from a viral upper respiratory infection when the parents administer aspirin for fever. The child subsequently develops persistent vomiting and altered mental status. To assess the severity of metabolic encephalopathy and risk of cerebral edema in suspected Reye Syndrome, which of the following is the most critical initial laboratory test?

A 6-year-old child presents with symptoms of pneumonia, including fever and productive cough. On examination, the child is found to be significantly underweight for his age and has bilateral wheezing on auscultation. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in the clinical evaluation to confirm the diagnosis and assess extent?

A neonate presents with signs of sepsis and meningitis, including bulging fontanelle and seizures. Imaging shows evidence of brainstem enhancement and basal meningitis. Which of the following organisms is a common cause of neonatal meningitis, particularly when there is a history of maternal consumption of unpasteurized dairy?

A 2-year-old child is brought to a primary health center. Upon assessment using the Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illness (IMNCI) guidelines, the health worker identifies that the child has a stiff neck and a high-grade fever. What is the correct IMNCI management for this "General Danger Sign"?

answers.option: Give a dose of appropriate antibiotic and refer urgently to the hospital
Start oral antibiotics and observe in the clinic for 4 hours
Perform a lumbar puncture in the clinic before referral
Treat for local infection and send home
Give oral paracetamol and ask the mother to return in 2 days

question: A 10-year-old boy presents with sudden onset of jaundice, dark-colored urine, and worsening anemia. He has a one-week history of fever with rigors and chills, for which he was prescribed an antimalarial drug in the OPD yesterday. Which of the following laboratory tests is most appropriate to confirm the underlying enzymatic deficiency?

A 4-year-old child is diagnosed with measles based on the presence of high-grade fever, cough, coryza, conjunctivitis, and a maculopapular rash. According to WHO guidelines, which of the following vitamins should be administered to all children with measles to reduce the risk of complications such as blindness and pneumonia?

A 13-year-old boy with a tall, slender build presents with sudden-onset shortness of breath and pleuritic chest pain that began while he was walking up the stairs. His respiratory rate is 32/min. Family history is significant for a maternal uncle who died suddenly in his early 20s. On examination, breath sounds are diminished on the right side. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old child is brought to the emergency department in significant respiratory distress. The child is drooling, febrile, and sitting in a "tripod" position (leaning forward with hands on knees). What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old girl presents with a one-month history of intermittent fever and cough. She has not received any routine vaccinations. On examination, her respiratory rate is 28/min and heart rate is 100/min; the rest of the physical exam is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step to screen for a common chronic infection in this high-risk patient?

A clinician is evaluating a pediatric patient for suspected infective endocarditis. According to the Modified Duke Criteria, a definitive clinical diagnosis can be made in the presence of which of the following?

answers.option: Two minor and one major criteria
One major and three minor criteria

question: A cyanotic newborn is evaluated for suspected congenital heart disease. Physical examination reveals an increased left ventricular impulse and a pansystolic murmur along the left sternal border. The ECG shows left axis deviation and left ventricular hypertrophy. What is the most likely diagnosis?

answers.option: Pulmonary atresia with intact ventricular septum

question: An 8-year-old child presents with persistent fever, bone pain, and significant hepatosplenomegaly. A CBC shows anemia and thrombocytopenia. A bone marrow biopsy is performed and reveals that 60% of the nucleated cells are blast cells. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old boy presents with progressive proximal muscle weakness and a positive Gower sign. Laboratory tests show a significantly elevated creatine kinase. Which of the following is the most common cause of mortality in patients with this condition during late adolescence or early adulthood?

A 12-year-old girl presents with a malar rash, recurrent oral ulcers, and symmetrical joint pain. Initial screening reveals a positive ANA. Which of the following antibodies is highly specific for this condition and is most useful for monitoring disease activity, particularly renal involvement?

An 18-month-old child presents with severe pallor, irritability, and poor growth. Physical examination reveals frontal bossing and hepatosplenomegaly. The parents report that the child has required monthly blood transfusions since the age of 6 months. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-day-old neonate, born at home without skilled attendance, is brought to the clinic due to persistent oozing of blood from the umbilical stump. The infant did not receive any intramuscular injections at birth. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A child with beta-thalassemia major has received over 20 units of packed red blood cells. His serum ferritin is now 2500 ng/mL. Which of the following medications is commonly used for iron chelation to prevent organ damage from secondary hemochromatosis?

A 3-year-old child is brought to the pediatrician after the mother noticed a large, firm, non-tender abdominal mass while bathing the child. The child is otherwise asymptomatic except for mild hypertension. What is the most common primary renal tumor in children?

A 10-year-old boy is evaluated for short stature. His height is below the 3rd percentile, but his growth velocity is normal. His IQ and physical examination are normal. A hand X-ray shows that his bone age is consistent with his chronological age. Both parents are also noted to be of shorter than average stature. What is the most likely diagnosis?

answers.option: Constitutional delay of growth and puberty

question: An adolescent is brought to the emergency department with pinpoint pupils, a respiratory rate of 6 breaths/min, and a depressed level of consciousness after an accidental overdose. Which of the following is the standard initial dose of the antagonist used to reverse opioid-induced respiratory depression?
